title: koine proposal
description: The proposal envelope — the day-one gesture (Law 2: an incoming version is a proposal; the field-wise conflict list IS the merge). A proposal is a standalone whole item; per Law 4 it never travels inside the target repo. Two grains, one envelope: a SHAPE proposal changes a definition's declarations; a BODY proposal carries target.selector and one change whose field is "body", and is how a live editor's text range and this envelope express each other.

path.description: The target's path at drafting time

baseContentHash.description: The target's contentHash the proposal was drafted against — staleness is mechanically detectable

selector.description: OPTIONAL Locator selector (SPEC 3.4) — where inside the addressed version the change lands. Required for a body proposal; its absence makes the proposal shape-grained.

baseChainHead.description: The history chain head at drafting time — a receiver can tell whether history moved since

schema.description: The declared record type the resulting shape is checked against (e.g. koine/types/metric-definition@v0)

proposer.description: Who proposes. Authorship is attributed, not proven — proving it is the signing chapter

when.description: ISO-8601 UTC (Z), as everywhere in koine

field.description: The declaration's key, or the reserved name "body" for a change to the addressed region of the body itself

from.description: Any JSON. OMIT the key to mean the field is absent on this side (an addition); null is the JSON value null, a different fact

to.description: Any JSON. OMIT the key to mean the field is absent on this side (a removal); null is the JSON value null, a different fact

changes.description: The field-wise diff this proposal intends — receipt recomputes it and must agree. A change omitting both from and to is not a change.

resultingShape.description: The complete shape after applying the changes; MUST validate against the declared record type. Absent for a body proposal — prose has no declared shape.

openQuestions.description: What the proposer could not decide — surfaced, never silently resolved
